prompt:
Image 1 is the target art style. Image 2 is a strip of the scroll 清明上河图 showing what lies beyond the edge of our walkable scene. Paint one wide panel of a painted backdrop, in exactly image 1's painting style (hand-inked dark-brown linework, light hatching, muted painted colours), showing the content of image 2 as a distant view seen from eye level, as if standing at the edge of our scene and looking out: the outer road running on east past the official hall, seen along it, every part of it small and far off: on the road two big family carts with high domed hoods of shaggy brown palm fibre on two tall spoked wheels, the far one drawn by two oxen, with drivers, a rider and a few walkers; on the left of the road a long hall on a raised floor with a dark blue cloth hanging along its eave, a crowd of men standing round a seated man, a wheelwright bent over a big cart wheel, three pack donkeys going up a lane, then a huge gnarled old tree, almost bare, over low mat-awning sheds and an open-fronted tea house full of tables and benches; at the far end of the road, on the left, a bank path with a few tiny porters and four or five big cargo boats with arched mat roofs moored side by side against the bank, only a short reach of the river showing round them, its water a deep blue-green much darker than the sky and drawn with fine ink ripple lines, the rest of it hidden behind low houses and bare trees on the bank; on the right the long tiled roofs of big halls one behind another, with a few bare trees; above and beyond all of it only the plain pale sky: no far trees, islands, hills, clouds or haze banks, no city wall, no pagoda.

Rules for the panel:
- Everything is far away (50 to 300 metres): small, soft, low in contrast, with gentle atmospheric haze; nothing large in the foreground and no people closer than the middle distance.
- The horizon sits about one third up from the bottom. The bottom fifth is pale, even mist over the ground, so the panel can meet a misty floor; the top is open pale sky, fading to near white at the top edge.
- The left and right ends dissolve into the same pale mist, so the panel can stand in a ring of mist.
- Colours are the real town's in soft spring daylight, muted and natural: grey-blue tiles, white plaster, weathered timber, tan earth, pale grey-green willows and bare ink-brown branches, a blue-grey distance. Not the yellow of aged silk, no paper texture, no border, no frame, no seal, no text, no signature.
